Reviewer Rationale: This is the clearest, most complete 'no relevant commitment found' case in the entire review — not merely a weak or opaque target, but a formally revoked one, with the accompanying net-zero long-term strategy also explicitly abandoned. CAT's own rating framework has shifted to directly assessing the absence of any target.

What to Assess: Specific methane reduction commitment vs IPCC rapid methane reduction requirement
NDC Source/Page: Inflation Reduction Act Waste Emissions Charge (WEC, methane fee rule); H.J.Res.35 (signed into law March 14, 2025); EPA Greenhouse Gas Reporting Program (GHGRP) proposed amendment (Sept 9, 2025)
NDC Evidence Excerpt: Congress used the Congressional Review Act to disapprove the EPA's WEC rule (which would have charged oil and gas producers $900–$1,500/tonne for excess methane emissions), and President Trump signed this into law in March 2025, voiding the regulation 'and limit[ing] the promulgating agency's discretion to re-promulgate a similar rule in the future' (Vinson & Elkins, secondary) — though the underlying IRA statutory obligation technically remains unrepealed with no enforceable mechanism. Separately, EPA proposed suspending most Greenhouse Gas Reporting Program obligations and 'delaying oil and gas methane reporting requirements until 2034' (Columbia Climate Law Blog, secondary) — a near-decade data blackout on the emissions data needed to implement any methane policy.
IPCC Source/Page: IPCC AR6 Synthesis Report SPM B.6.2
IPCC Evidence Excerpt: 1.5°C (>50%) no/limited-overshoot pathways: global methane emissions reduced 34% [21–57%] by 2030 relative to 2019.
Reviewer Rationale: Both the market-based methane fee mechanism and the underlying emissions-reporting infrastructure needed to implement any methane policy have been legislatively repealed or administratively suspended — this is an active dismantling, not merely an absence of ambition.

What to Assess: Quantified adaptation finance needs/commitments and conditionality
NDC Source/Page: Executive Order 14162 (Jan 2025); OBBBA (July 2025), termination of the Greenhouse Gas Reduction Fund
NDC Evidence Excerpt: Woodwell Climate Research Center (secondary) states directly: 'The executive order is targeted at stopping any U.S. climate finance contributions,' which would include international adaptation finance previously provided by the US. Domestically, OBBBA 'terminated the Greenhouse Gas Reduction Fund, which was also created under the Inflation Reduction Act and provided billions of dollars in investments' (NYC Independent Budget Office, secondary) in climate resilience and clean energy financing.
IPCC Source/Page: IPCC AR6 WGII SPM C.3, C.5
IPCC Evidence Excerpt: AR6 WGII documents a widening adaptation finance gap; most tracked climate finance still goes to mitigation, and adaptation finance falls short of documented needs in developing countries.
Reviewer Rationale: Both international climate finance contributions and a major domestic resilience-funding mechanism have been explicitly halted or statutorily terminated in 2025, consistent with the rubric's definition of Absent.

What to Assess: Loss and Damage finance needs, liability/compensation references, or related commitments
NDC Source/Page: Executive Order 14162 (Jan 2025)
NDC Evidence Excerpt: No loss-and-damage finance need, liability/compensation reference, or fund contribution exists — the executive order withdrawing from the Paris Agreement is 'targeted at stopping any U.S. climate finance contributions' (Woodwell Climate, secondary), which would encompass any prior or planned L&D Fund engagement.
IPCC Evidence Excerpt: AR6 WGII recognizes losses and damages as escalating, unequally distributed, and worsening with each increment of warming, with hard/soft adaptation limits already reached in some systems.
Reviewer Rationale: No relevant commitment found, directly and explicitly confirmed by the executive order's stated intent to halt all US climate finance contributions.

What to Assess: Transport electrification/modal shift/sector target vs IPCC transport mitigation pathway
NDC Source/Page: EPA Endangerment Finding repeal (proposed, final decision expected ~Jan 2026); vehicle GHG emissions standards rescission; OBBBA (EV tax credit repeal); NEVI program suspension
NDC Evidence Excerpt: EPA has moved to rescind the 2009 Endangerment Finding, the legal basis for federal GHG vehicle standards, and has 'formally rescinded a host of federal GHG emissions standards for trucks and automobiles' (Legal Planet, secondary) — standards that 'would have led to EVs constituting approximately 68% of new automobile sales nationwide by 2032.' OBBBA repealed EV tax credits (25E, 30D, 45W) for vehicles acquired after Sept 30, 2025, and the 30C charging-infrastructure credit after June 30, 2026. The Federal Highway Administration rescinded all guidance for the National EV Infrastructure (NEVI) formula grant program and suspended all state NEVI plan approvals (Plug In America, secondary). CAFE fuel-economy violation penalties were also zeroed out.
IPCC Evidence Excerpt: 1.5°C (no/limited overshoot) pathways require a 59% [42–68%] reduction in transport CO2 by 2050 vs modelled 2020 levels; light-duty-vehicle electrification is the leading near-term lever.
Reviewer Rationale: This is a comprehensive, multi-pronged rollback: the legal basis for vehicle emissions standards, the tax credits supporting EV adoption, the charging infrastructure funding, and fuel-economy enforcement penalties have all been eliminated within 2025 — a fundamentally different picture from every other country reviewed, where transport policy was at worst underambitious rather than actively dismantled.

What to Assess: Land-use commitments, sink accounting, additionality, and offsets
NDC Source/Page: No current NDC exists (revoked, Jan 2025)
NDC Evidence Excerpt: No LULUCF accounting methodology, sink target, or additionality safeguard currently exists at the federal level, as the entire NDC framework that would have specified this treatment was formally revoked. No LULUCF-specific rollback announcement was separately identified, but this follows directly from the blanket revocation of the underlying NDC document itself.
IPCC Evidence Excerpt: AFOLU can provide 20–30% of global mitigation needed for 1.5/2°C pathways to 2050 (~8–14 GtCO2e/yr economic potential), led by forest/ecosystem protection; the chapter flags long-term additionality and permanence uncertainty for land-sink-heavy strategies.
Reviewer Rationale: Consistent with the across-the-board revocation of the US NDC, there is no operative LULUCF target to evaluate. Confidence is Medium rather than High because no LULUCF-specific rollback action was separately confirmed in searches — the classification follows by direct logical consequence of the NDC's blanket revocation rather than a dimension-specific news event.
